items.subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)
items.stimulus: Amateur astronomers who join variable-star monitoring programs are often ______ the photometry software that professional observatories use. The obstacle is not attitude: most volunteers, once shown the software, adopt it readily. It is that many have spent decades estimating a star's brightness by eye against printed comparison charts, a method that requires no calibration files at all. items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: The text rules out an attitude problem ('The obstacle is not attitude') and points to inexperience instead. A.why: This is the vivid-attitude trap. Amateurs who trust their eyes might seem to distrust software, but the text says outright that the obstacle is not attitude and that volunteers adopt the software readily.

B.why: You took 'decades' of experience as skill with the software. That experience was with eye estimates and printed charts, and the month of training shows the volunteers are not yet skilled with the software.

D.why: The volunteers have spent decades on a different method. Nothing shows devotion to software they haven't used yet, and the need for training shows they haven't.

items.subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)
items.stimulus: Court composer Anselm Ritter was, at most, ______ the sharp dissonances his younger pupils favored. items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

B.why: You correctly noticed that Ritter used dissonances himself, then took that as enthusiasm. 'At most', 'a spice, not a meal', and their limited use at cadences all cap his feeling well below delight.

C.why: Someone opposed to dissonances would not let them stand in pupils' work or put them in his own sonatas.

D.why: Ritter wrote about the dissonances in his letters and used them in his scores, so he clearly knew about them.

items.subtype_name: Word + preposition choices (attitude or ability toward something)
items.stimulus: Because the eighteenth-century mapmaker Marguerite Dalloz never visited the interior valleys she charted, relying instead on traders' spoken accounts, she was understandably ______ the distances between settlements. Her manuscript map shows this plainly: beside every distance she recorded the name of the trader who supplied it and a small "c." for circa, and where two traders disagreed, she wrote both figures.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: 'Because' ties the blank to the fact that she relied on secondhand reports, and 'understandably' tells you the reaction is a reasonable one. Her map backs this up: she marks figures as approximate, names her sources, and records disagreements. She was 'uncertain about' the distances, and she was careful to show it.

A.why: The 'c.' markings and the conflicting figures she recorded side by side show doubt, not confidence.

C.why: This is the trap. You saw that her information was secondhand and chose a strong negative word. But recording sources, marking approximations, and keeping both disputed figures is the reverse of carelessness.

D.why: Someone indifferent to the distances would not track who supplied each one or note where traders disagreed.

items.stimulus: Early twentieth-century excavators at Tell Qaran were largely ______ the site's fragmentary bone awls. They logged the awls in a single line of the register, without measurements or drawings, and discarded most of them, saving their attention for intact pottery. items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

items.stimulus: Repeated exposure seems to leave athletes ______ crowd noise. In laboratory trials, sprinters who had competed in large stadiums showed no change in reaction time when a recorded roar played, whereas novices started measurably later. items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Two conditions must hold together. The veterans' performance did not change, and they still noticed the noise, since their heart rates rose. They registered the noise without being thrown by it, which is 'unfazed by'.

A.why: This trap survives the first insight. You correctly saw that the noise had no effect on performance, then concluded the veterans didn't notice it. The rising heart rates and 'not tuning the sound out' rule that out.

B.why: The veterans showed 'no change in reaction time', not an improvement. A rising heart rate alone doesn't show that the noise helped them.

C.why: This describes the novices, who started later. The blank is about experienced athletes, whose starts were not disrupted.
